section_summary: This section documents Allied investigations and policy planning regarding the custody, examination, and preservation of Japanese diplomatic, consular, public, and commercial archives immediately following the surrender of Japan in September 1945. It includes diplomatic correspondence from Port-au-Prince, Panama, Baghdad, Havana, and Beirut detailing local inspections of Japanese consulate files, annotated military maps, and negotiations concerning the seizure of Japanese public and private property. Additionally, the section features an extensive Foreign Economic Administration report (LM-4) providing comprehensive recommendations on safeguarding Japanese government, financial, industrial, and technical records to support Allied occupation administration, property restitution, war crimes prosecution, and industrial disarmament.

subfiles.about: Examination of the archives of the Japanese Consulate at Port-au-Prince covering 1935 to 1941, kept by former Honorary Consul Edouard Estève.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Wainwright Abbott reports on the examination of consular files held by Edouard Estève, Haitian citizen and former Honorary Japanese Consul from 1935 until his resignation in 1941. The archives contained trade statistics sent to the Japanese Legation in Havana, correspondence on Japanese exports and a 1936 trade mission involving Takaharu Itō and K. Mitsuzani, a 1939 Japanese request for Haitian passport models, scrap iron inquiries from Iwai and Company, and Estève's refusal in 1942 to deliver files to Spanish representatives Manuel Acal y Marín and Daniel G. Marcos. An accompanying State Department routing slip records distribution of the despatch to MID, ONI, FBI, and OSS.
subfiles.title: Examination of Archives of Japanese Consulate at Port-au-Prince

subfiles.about: Transmittal of an annotated map of Panama discovered in seized Japanese archives, detailing military and geographic pencil markings.
subfiles.summary: Third Secretary of Embassy V. Lansing Collins, Jr. transmits a map of the Republic of Panama recovered from Japanese archives made available by the Panamanian government. The despatch catalogs twenty-nine specific handwritten annotations, auxiliary road tracings, circled areas, and penciled names across Chiriquí, Bocas del Toro, Veraguas, Los Santos, Coclé, and Darién, requesting that a United States intelligence agency perform a more detailed analysis. A State Department transmittal slip confirms circulation of copies to MID, ONI, FBI, and OSS, with the original map retained in Department files.
subfiles.title: Transmitting Map of Republic of Panamá Found in Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Request for instructions regarding joint Allied custody with British and Soviet colleagues over Japanese archives and public property in Iraq.
subfiles.summary: American representative Moreland in Baghdad reports that his British and Soviet colleagues have received instructions to assume joint custody with him over all Japanese consular and diplomatic archives and public property in Iraq as soon as the protecting power receives the necessary instructions. Moreland requests immediate instructions from the Department of State.
subfiles.title: Joint Custody of Japanese Consular and Diplomatic Archives and Public Property in Iraq

subfiles.about: Comprehensive policy report and errata outlining methods and requirements for safeguarding, seizing, and using Japanese public, corporate, financial, and technical records during occupation.
subfiles.summary: Transmitted to Charles P. Taft by Constance G. Gaynor of the Foreign Economic Administration, FEA Report No. LM-4 (Enemy Branch, August 1945, with September 1945 errata) presents exhaustive guidelines for preserving and exploiting Japanese records. The study details the critical necessity of records for occupation administration, restitution of confiscated Allied property, apprehension of war criminals, and industrial disarmament, proposing military custody, vault sealing, impoundment, and penal ordinances. It surveys record-keeping across Cabinet boards, ministries, prefectural governments, police departments, quasi-governmental control bodies (Tōsei-kai, Eidan, National Policy Companies), financial organs, and mechanized installations, concluding with extensive reference appendices listing administrative regions, key industrial combines, banks, and scientific research institutes.
subfiles.title: Preservation and Use of Key Records in Japan (FEA Report No. LM-4)

subfiles.about: Report on the examination by the Cuban Ministry of State of sealed boxes of Japanese Legation archives and property received from Spain.
subfiles.summary: American Ambassador R. Henry Norweb reports from Havana that the Cuban Ministry of State completed its inspection of sealed boxes delivered by the Spanish Chargé representing all property taken over from the Japanese Legation. Except for several thousand cards apparently forming a registration file, no archives material was found. Norweb doubts the ability of former Cuban Consul Vidal to translate the cards and recommends that a concise analysis await an American specialist in written Japanese.
subfiles.title: Examination of Japanese Legation Archives and Property in Cuba

subfiles.about: French diplomatic protest concerning the transfer of Japanese archives and property in the Levant without French consultation and participation.
subfiles.summary: The French Government expresses surprise that United States Minister George Wadsworth at Beirut, acting jointly with British, Soviet, and Chinese colleagues, obtained custody of Japanese diplomatic and consular archives from the Spanish Consulate and is preparing to request the surrender of all Japanese property in Syria and Lebanon without consulting French Delegate General General Étienne Beynet. France requests that instructions be sent to Wadsworth to admit the French representative to the negotiations immediately. Additionally, France requests information on United States intentions regarding the disposition of Japanese public and private property outside Japan, expressing its desire to participate in measures taken in non-belligerent nations.
subfiles.title: Aide-Mémoire on Japanese Diplomatic and Consular Archives and Property in Syria and Lebanon
